scope: Current V1 preparation and owned accepted-outcome recovery; partial system requirements, not M03 acceptance.

behavior.claim: A player-locked transaction reserves a unique computing attempt for (game, revision) before computation. Another live claimant receives SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE and retries the same command. Claims expire after 30 seconds; publication fences by unique attempt ID.
behavior.results: Ready jobs are reused before calculation without changing result or expiry. New authorization/expiry attempts use fresh receipt IDs; original issued results and expiry remain in preparation_attempts. jobs retains UNIQUE(game_id,revision).
behavior.publication: Revalidate owner/session, active game, current coverage, captured access generation, control lease, revision, observation, decision identity, policy and claim expiry before publication. Commit checks access generation/control again.
behavior.hearts: One atomic human-plus-three-bot pass bundle; starting access generation is rechecked. Human transitions now save the complete final game document once in the transaction.
behavior.reconciliation: Exact owned accepted command replay precedes new-work guards and computation. GET /api/commands/:commandId returns accepted/unknown; GET /api/review-trials/:commandId returns an owned already-ready public trial only. Receipt reads do not load or project unsupported active state. Current safe session is fetched separately by the client.

primaryCheck.sourceStage: Initial repair before the independently reviewed expiry-clock and legacy-forced corrections below.
coverage: Two service instances reserve one compute and reuse ready result/expiry; eight concurrent same-command advances accept once.
Revoke/regrant, lease transfer, game replacement, revision advance and expiry during compute publish no result, events or audit.
A reclaimed expired claim publishes a different fixture result; late first worker cannot replace it.
Expired/access-changed/control-changed receipt gets a fresh ID and retains original result and expiry; old ID cannot advance.
Hearts revoke/regrant during sealed passing preserves all four original hands and records.
Accepted action/advice/unlock reconcile after replacement and expired coverage; fresh work remains denied and foreign/revoked sessions cannot recover.
Owned status and public ready trial are readable with unsupported active state; foreign status is unknown and foreign trial is 404.
Original policy/advice/audit tests and full Solo/Partners hands remain passing; searched analysis is outside transactions.

preliminaryCheck.classification: Test fixture error: fabricated stored ReviewTrial used worker-result fields instead of the public DTO, so response validation correctly returned 503. Fixture corrected before the primary passing run. This is not pre-repair defect reproduction.

additionalCheck.failure: Both failures were connect ETIMEDOUT 127.0.0.1:54330: first access-review test failed creating its isolated schema; integration file failed during top-level migrate. Integration cases did not execute.
additionalCheck.passedCoverage: Remaining nine access-review cases, including saved/expired advice, historical unlock, unavailable/expired/reclaimed trial attempts and saved trial after coverage expiry.

changes: All V1 preparation TTL creation and comparisons now use clock_timestamp(), so a transaction that waits for the player lock cannot use its earlier start time to publish or commit expired work.
Reused legacy action-only singleton decisions retain forced provenance without recomputation or changing stored job bytes/expiry.

lockWaitRegression.method: Pause immediately before the publication player lock, shorten the claim to 200 milliseconds, hold the player row in a separate PostgreSQL transaction, assert pg_stat_activity reports a Lock wait, cross the expiry, then release. Assert no receipt/job/event/audit/game mutation is published.

red.failure: Missing expected rejection: the expired result was published while now() still represented the transaction start.

lockWaitRegression.harnessCorrection: The first diagnostic run was interrupted because the dedicated blocker connection was released by a later teardown hook, after pool.end. Cleanup moved into finally before the meaningful red/green runs.

identityCompositionCorrection.behavior: GET /api/identity returns the generated closed IdentityView {playerId:string}. It uses the existing authenticated request context and ownedTransaction(loadGame:false), so ownership verification does not decode quarantined active state. It returns no account profile, access, game data or lease token and never creates an identity. AccountView validation remains unchanged.
identityCompositionCorrection.boundaryCoverage: Null/corrupt and unknown-game state; exact owned ID only and no game mutation; another session returns only its own ID; caller playerId query rejects; foreign Origin rejects; missing/revoked/expired sessions reject; no cookie or new player on unauthenticated calls.

red.failure: Missing endpoint returned 404 instead of the required owned identity.

limits: No live provider calls, model promotion, policy/rule/default changes, hosting, Go code, capacity test or completed V2 platform migration.
Computation remains synchronous on the Node event loop; the short claim TTL fences publication but does not interrupt CPU. General worker isolation and capacity admission remain pending.
Issued old receipts remain historical outcomes; status unknown is not proof that an in-flight mutation has failed.
The tests use two GameService instances sharing PostgreSQL and explicit barriers, not two independent OS server processes.

The initial 13-case focused suite has no controlled pre-fix red run; the later expiry-clock regression has a recorded red/green pair. Full integration and browser acceptance are owned by the parent task and not claimed by this artifact.
